memory_annotations.evidence_summary: No recurring travel preference was intentionally established. The session records only trip-specific choices: an earlier Monday arrival for installation preparation, two provisional return options, and a request to wait for the lender inspection schedule before selecting one.

messages.content: I need to start planning a Kansas City work trip for the collection installation. The crate opening is Tuesday morning, January 12, so I need to fly from Atlanta on Monday the 11th. The lender inspection is Thursday, but I do not know yet whether I can leave that evening or need to stay until Friday.
I can compare a Monday outbound with both return scenarios. What time is the Tuesday crate opening, and do you have a required check-in time at the museum beforehand?
The crate opening is at 9:00 a.m. I need to be there by 8:15. I would rather arrive Monday with enough time to check in, eat, and review the condition-report packet instead of landing late at night.

Understood. I’ll focus on Monday flights that reach Kansas City by early evening and then separately identify Thursday-evening and Friday-morning returns. Is this for one traveler, and should I search only nonstop service or include connections?
One traveler, just me. Start with nonstops. The art shipment is not traveling with me; the museum’s carrier is handling it separately.

For Monday, January 11, I found three nonstop economy choices from Atlanta to Kansas City. All times are local:

- Delta: 9:40 a.m. to 11:02 a.m., $438 round trip when paired with the currently available return choices.
- Southwest: 1:05 p.m. to 2:35 p.m., $401 round trip, with two checked bags included.
- Delta: 3:20 p.m. to 4:43 p.m., $424 round trip.

The morning flight provides the largest recovery margin, while the 1:05 p.m. departure still leaves most of Monday evening free. The 3:20 p.m. flight is workable but gives less protection against a delay. Which outbound should I examine more closely?
The 1:05 Southwest flight sounds reasonable. How long is it, and is that arrival time Central?

Yes. It departs Atlanta at 1:05 p.m. Eastern and arrives Kansas City at 2:35 p.m. Central. Scheduled elapsed time is 2 hours 30 minutes. That would put you in Kansas City more than seventeen hours before the 8:15 a.m. museum arrival requirement.
That margin is fine. Compare it with the 9:40 Delta on practical grounds, including what happens if either flight is canceled. I do not need you to price the shipment or add any freight arrangements.

The 9:40 a.m. Delta flight gives you an additional 3 hours 33 minutes in Kansas City and more same-day alternatives if the original flight is disrupted. Delta has later nonstop Atlanta-Kansas City service that day, so a cancellation could still allow reaccommodation without a connection, subject to available seats.

The 1:05 p.m. Southwest flight arrives at 2:35 p.m. and leaves ample preparation time, but there are fewer remaining nonstop recovery opportunities afterward. Its current fare is $37 lower and includes checked bags. Neither option involves the art shipment; I am treating this strictly as your passenger itinerary.
Let’s use the 9:40 Delta as the outbound we are considering. I would rather have the earlier arrival for this installation. Now show me what Thursday evening looks like after 6:00 p.m.

With the Monday 9:40 a.m. outbound, the Thursday, January 14 nonstop return choices after 6:00 p.m. are:

- Delta at 6:25 p.m. Central, arriving Atlanta at 9:30 p.m. Eastern; round-trip total $438.
- Southwest at 7:10 p.m. Central, arriving Atlanta at 10:15 p.m. Eastern; combining carriers would require separate one-way tickets totaling $472.

There is also a 5:35 p.m. Delta departure arriving at 8:40 p.m., but that is before your requested window. The 6:25 p.m. option is the cleanest single-ticket pairing.
The inspection is tentatively supposed to finish at 3:30, but that is not firm. How much time would I realistically have for the 6:25 flight?

If the inspection ends at 3:30 p.m., you would have 2 hours 55 minutes until departure. Allowing roughly 30 minutes to wrap up and leave the museum, then about 25 to 35 minutes by car to Kansas City International in ordinary traffic, you could reach the airport around 4:25 to 4:35 p.m. That leaves about 1 hour 50 minutes before departure. It is comfortable if the inspection ends on schedule, but a delay of an hour or more would narrow the margin substantially.

Right, and lender inspections can run over. What are the Friday morning nonstop choices? I would need enough time Thursday night to close out the paperwork, but I do not want to lose the whole next day.

For Friday, January 15, the useful nonstop morning returns are:

- Delta at 7:05 a.m. Central, arriving Atlanta at 10:10 a.m. Eastern; $421 round trip with the selected Monday outbound.
- Southwest at 8:20 a.m. Central, arriving Atlanta at 11:25 a.m. Eastern; separate-ticket total $455.
- Delta at 10:15 a.m. Central, arriving Atlanta at 1:20 p.m. Eastern; $447 round trip.

The 7:05 departure preserves the most of Friday but requires an early airport departure. The 10:15 option allows a less compressed morning while still reaching Atlanta in the early afternoon.
For the Delta options, are those Main Cabin fares or Basic Economy? I need to know what we are actually comparing.

The quoted Delta totals are Main Cabin, not Basic Economy. They include advance seat selection and standard carry-on allowance. A checked bag would be extra unless covered through another benefit. The fares are currently changeable without a change fee, although any fare difference would apply.
Good. Check the Friday 10:15 flight for aisle-seat availability, but do not assign or hold anything.

The Friday 10:15 a.m. Delta nonstop currently shows several standard Main Cabin aisle seats available, including seats in the middle and rear portions of the cabin. That is live availability only; no seat has been selected and no itinerary is being held.

Then keep the Monday 9:40 outbound in view. For the return, retain the Thursday 6:25 and Friday 10:15 possibilities. I should have the lender’s confirmed inspection schedule by the end of this week, so I do not want to choose between them yet.

I’ve kept the comparison open with no booking or hold: Monday, January 11, Delta Main Cabin nonstop from Atlanta at 9:40 a.m. Eastern, arriving Kansas City at 11:02 a.m. Central. The two return possibilities are Thursday, January 14 at 6:25 p.m. Central, arriving Atlanta at 9:30 p.m. Eastern, for a current round-trip total of $438, or Friday, January 15 at 10:15 a.m. Central, arriving at 1:20 p.m. Eastern, for $447. The Friday flight currently has standard aisle seats available. Fares and seats must be rechecked after the lender inspection time is confirmed; nothing has been ticketed, selected, or held.
